newsitem.title: PERU: Embassy security was lax, Peruvian rebel leader says.
newsitem.headline: Embassy security was lax, Peruvian rebel leader says.

text.p: "Incredible" lapses in security made it easy for Peruvian guerrillas to seize the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima and take about 500 hostages, the rebel who led the assault has been quoted as saying.

Guerrilla leader Nestor Cerpa's assessment of security precautions at the residence was contained in the diary of Peruvian economist Francisco Sagasti, one of about 420 hostages released since the spectacular Dec. 17 raid.
"Cerpa ... mentioned that there were incredible security lapses at the embassy," Sagasti wrote in a diary published in the latest issue of the weekly magazine Caretas.
He quoted Cerpa as saying, "We went to the trouble of preparing an ambulance for the assault, but that turned out to have been unnecessary, because there were no police in the back street."
The original plan of the rebels, members of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement, was to drive into the grounds of the residence in the back of an ambulance.
Instead, they blew a hole in the back wall and swarmed in through the garden.
